original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-n-skeleton-sets}
Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The morphism $i_{n!} \text{sk}_n U \to U$ identifies
$i_{n!} \text{sk}_n U$ with the simplicial set
$U' \subset U$ defined in Lemma \ref{lemma-simplicial-set-n-skel-sub}.

reviewed_content.statement:
Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The morphism $i_{n!} \text{sk}_n U \to U$ identifies
$i_{n!} \text{sk}_n U$ with the simplicial subset \(U'\subseteq U\) with \(U'_r=\bigcup_{\varphi:[r]\to[i],\ i\le n}\operatorname{Im}(U(\varphi):U_i\to U_r)\) for every \(r\ge0\).
hypotheses:
Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
conclusions: The canonical map \(i_{n!}\operatorname{sk}_nU\to U\) identifies \(i_{n!}\operatorname{sk}_nU\) with the simplicial subset \(U'\subseteq U\) whose \(r\)-simplices are \(U'_r=\bigcup_{\varphi:[r]\to[i],\,i\le n}\operatorname{Im}(U(\varphi):U_i\to U_r)\).
